newsitem.title: UK: UK MPs attack OFGAS over British Gas index.
newsitem.headline: UK MPs attack OFGAS over British Gas index.

text.p: A parliamentary committee on Thursday attacked Britain's gas industry regulator for having introduced changes to British Gas Plc's price control system four years ago without considering some viable alternatives.

The powerful Public Accounts Committee said in a report the changes had benefited the company by millions of pounds a year compared with either continuing with the old regime or adopting the one alternative which the regulator, OFGAS, did look at.

It criticised OFGAS for failing to document important parts of their work in developing the "gas cost index" -- designed to ensure retail gas prices reflected the fluctuating price British Gas had to pay for its gas supplies -- instituted in 1992.
Before that year, British Gas had simply passed on changes in the prices it paid via a "cost pass through" system.

Under the new regime, the "gas-costs element" was calculated according to an index based on factors such as movements in fuel oil prices, giving British Gas an incentive to negotiate better supply contracts.
But the report said that in the first two years of the new regime, British Gas's average gas costs were about three percent below the level of these control factors.
"On the company's forecasts in June 1995, the difference between the two was expected to total some 250 million stg over the period covered by the control," the report said.

"It is likely that if cost pass-through had been retained, the gas cost element of the prices paid by customers would have been lower as a result, but with the adoption of the gas cost index, British Gas has benefited instead," it said.
"We recommend that in the future OFGAS should be more attentive to the need for price controls to be robust in a range of external conditions."

The committee noted that from April next year, OFGAS was now proposing to revert to the "cost pass-through" system, but would require British Gas to show their proposed charges represented value for money.

It said that in 1992, OFGAS had considered another basis for the price control which, according to the National Audit Office, would have cost British Gas an average of 33 million stg a year over five years.

"We are concerned that in devising the gas-cost index as a replacement for cost pass through OFGAS did not consider formally, or in detail, a number of other options that appear to have had merit," its report said.
"We are very concerned that OFGAS did not document important parts of their work in developing the gas cost index.

"We consider it essential that public bodies keep adequate records of the reasons for their decisions, to help ensure the proper conduct of public business and for accountability," it added. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
